title: Security Model (Authoring Intent)
description:
IMPORTANT — READ BEFORE USING THIS SCHEMA.

Nothing in this model grants, widens, or enforces access. A page definition is a statement of intent, never a security boundary. Definitions are authored by business users and generated by a language model; both are untrusted with respect to entitlements, and a stored definition may have been hand-edited, copied between tenants, or produced by a hallucination.

Enforcement happens server-side, in the Data Gateway, resolved from the caller's identity at request time, independently of anything declared here. If this model and the gateway disagree, the gateway wins and this model is ignored.

What this model is for: (1) declaring who an experience is intended for, so the platform can hide what is irrelevant rather than showing a wall of denied widgets; (2) declaring how a page should behave when entitlement is absent; (3) declaring the sensitivity a page exposes, so a reviewer approves with knowledge of what the page reveals. All three are usability and governance concerns, not access control.

Two authorization axes exist and are orthogonal. Platform authorization — what you may do in the Studio — is owned by Experience Studio and is what 'capabilities' and 'roles' below refer to. Data authorization — which rows and columns you may see — is owned by EDM and is never expressed in this model at all.

artifactSecurity.description: Security intent for an experience or page.

intendedAudience.description: Free-text statement of who this is for. Documentation for reviewers; carries no enforcement.

requiredRoles.description: Platform roles whose absence hides this artifact from navigation and search. A user who reaches it by direct URL is still checked server-side; this list is a filter, not a gate.

requiredCapabilities.description: Platform capabilities required to open this artifact, e.g. 'experience.view', 'export.data'.

workspaceScope.description: Sharing tier. Governance weight scales with this value: a personal artifact publishes instantly, a production artifact requires review and separation of duties. Proportionate governance is a security control — uniform friction gets routed around.

deniedDataPolicy.description: Default behaviour for widgets whose data the caller may not see. 'showDeniedState' is the recommended default: silently hiding widgets makes a page look complete when it is not, whereas 'not available to you' is honest and legible. Individual components may override.

sensitivityDeclaration.description: Highest sensitivity classification this artifact binds, together with the contributing references. COMPUTED by the platform at validation time from the catalog, not authored — an author cannot understate it. Surfaced to reviewers at publication so approval is informed rather than ceremonial.

exportPolicy.description: Constraints on data leaving the platform. Every other control applies to data on a screen; an export leaves the perimeter entirely, so it is governed separately and always audited.

watermark.description: Stamp exports with user, timestamp and classification.

auditProfile.description: 'elevated' records an audit event for every view of this artifact, not only for data queries. Appropriate for pages over restricted data.

allowCopy.description: Whether other authors may duplicate this artifact as a starting point.

allowTemplate.description: Whether it may be promoted to a template. Distinct from exemplarEligible: a template may be instantiable within a tenant without being usable as an AI exemplar across tenants.

allowCrossTenantExemplar.description: Whether this artifact may serve as an AI few-shot exemplar outside its owning tenant. Defaults to false and may only be set true by a Template Curator on a scrubbed, platform-curated artifact. A client's dashboard describes that client's data model, naming and operational concerns, so cross-tenant exemplar use leaks commercially sensitive structure without touching a single data row — the least obvious leak path in the platform.

elementSecurity.description: Security intent for one element — a component, tab, action, navigation item or layout region. Same rule as above: this hides things, it does not protect them.

rationale.description: Why this restriction exists. Recorded for reviewers, because an unexplained restriction is usually removed by the next author who finds it inconvenient.

platformRole.description: Platform role. Closed set: these are defined by the platform's own authorization model, and an unknown role must be a validation error rather than a silently-unsatisfiable condition. Data entitlements are NOT roles and never appear here.

capability.description: Fine-grained platform permission, '<resource>.<action>'. Open string because the capability set grows with the platform; unknown capabilities are rejected by semantic validation against the platform's capability registry rather than by this schema.

lifecycleTransitionPolicy.description: Tenant-level policy governing how artifacts move toward production. Stored with tenant configuration, not inside artifacts; defined here because it belongs to the security model.

separationOfDuties.description: When true, an author may not approve their own artifact for production. Tenant-configurable because some clients accept the risk and others are contractually forbidden from doing so.

blockPublishOnSensitivityAbove.description: Sensitivity above which publication requires an additional named approver.
